questions.stem: Define heterolytic fission and name both products in general terms.
questions.modelAnswer: Heterolytic fission breaks a covalent bond so both bonding electrons go to one atom, producing a positive ion (cation) and a negative ion (anion).

questions.stem: Write the heterolytic fission equation for H-Br and label each product.
questions.modelAnswer: H-Br -> H(+) + Br(-): the hydrogen becomes the cation and bromine the anion.

questions.stem: Explain why the products of heterolytic fission are reactive.
questions.modelAnswer: The products are ions carrying full charges, so each is a ready donor or acceptor of electron pairs - the nucleophile and electrophile pairing that drives ionic mechanisms.

questions.stem: A polar bond A-B breaks with both electrons going to B. State the charge and role of each fragment.
questions.modelAnswer: B becomes the anion B(-) and acts as a nucleophile (pair donor); A becomes the cation A(+) and acts as an electrophile (pair acceptor).

options.explanation: That is an ionic species, not a radical.

options.explanation: The unpaired electron defines it.

options.text: A charged ion with a full octet
options.explanation: Radicals are neutral and electron-short.

options.text: A molecule with all electrons paired
options.explanation: Paired electrons mean no radical.

questions.stem: How is a chlorine free radical written?

options.explanation: That would be a cation.
The dot must appear for the radical.

options.text: Cl•, with a single dot for the unpaired electron
options.explanation: The dot is the radical's signature.
That is the chloride ion.

questions.stem: Define homolytic fission and write the equation for chlorine undergoing it.
questions.modelAnswer: Homolytic fission splits a covalent bond with one electron going to each atom, forming radicals: Cl2 -> 2Cl• under ultraviolet light.

questions.stem: State what notation marks a radical and what energy source typically starts homolytic fission.
questions.modelAnswer: A single dot marks the unpaired electron, and ultraviolet light typically supplies the energy for the split.

questions.stem: Explain why homolytic rather than heterolytic fission occurs in a non-polar bond like Cl-Cl.
questions.modelAnswer: The identical atoms share the pair evenly, so there is no electronegativity tilt to hand the pair to one side - the symmetric bond breaks symmetrically when energy is supplied.

questions.stem: Bromine gas is irradiated with ultraviolet light. Write the homolytic fission equation with correct radical notation and state what each product carries.
questions.modelAnswer: Br2 -> 2Br•: each bromine radical is a neutral atom carrying one unpaired electron, marked by the single dot.
